findings.title: Constructor accepts loose public options type, losing compile-time validation
findings.body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Previously the discriminated union type required `teamId` when scope is "team". Callers can now pass `scope: "team"` without a `teamId` and the code still compiles. At runtime, safeParse then fails and the service silently returns `1=0`, so callers get empty results with no error to point at the bad call.

findings.title: findMany removed without migrating callers
findings.body: The public `findMany` method is replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, such as insights routers, will break. Each caller now has to hand-write a raw query, and the PR does not update any of them.

findings.title: Integration test relies on denormalized view and dropped caching tests
findings.body: The caching tests were deleted even though the caching logic is still in the service, so that behaviour is no longer covered. The PR author also admits the tests were never run. The new `$queryRaw` test assumes the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` view exposes exactly these columns. Because nothing was executed, the SQL fragments' compatibility with the view (column quoting, `ANY` with int arrays) has not been verified.
